candidates.summary: Routing $$, \\( and \\[ through findClose gives their closer search a link-destination skip that ends only at a balanced ')': a formula holding '[..](' with no ')' before its closer misses that closer and runs on to a later one, swallowing the links after it
candidates.failure_scenario: `\\( [a,b](x \\) and [l](/r/y) then \\(z\\)`: the depth tracker takes the ')' of the closer \\) as the destination's end, so the closer's first byte is never tested, and the formula runs to the last \\): one formula ' [a,b](x \\) and [l](/r/y) then \\(z', and the link /r/y is gone. `$$[0,1](x $$ and [l](/r/y) z` + newline + `w $$`: no closer on line 1, so the formula takes the next line's closer and swallows the link. The ADR's own example `$$[0,1](x$$ then $$y$$` renders as plain text with no formula. The merge base closed each at the first closer, so all three rendered the formulas and the link. A CommonMark destination cannot hold a space or run past its line, so the scanner treats as a link a span goldmark never would

candidates.failure_scenario: A realm renders `[Send $10](/r/demo/bank$help&func=Send)` + newline + `Balance: 100$`. findClose returns -1 at the label's '](' (the point the closeScan doc calls one 'no expression crosses'), but findCloseCached hands Parse only the -1, and Parse runs the line-2 search (line 204). That search finds '100$', so the whole link and 'Balance: 100' render as one formula, '10](/r/demo/bank$help&func=Send)\nBalance: 100', and the visitor loses the Send link.
